findings.message: PRD 4.9 'Awaiting your approval since <time> (<age>)' is implemented as `awaiting-since` in AwaitingNotice (src/projects/node/ControllerSections.tsx, rendered only when the node has a status row) but no test exercises it: controller-panels (tests/project-workflows/ux-review.spec.ts:162-165) uses RUN_AWAITING_APPROVAL, which has no status row, so the branch never renders in either phase, and no spec references `awaiting-since`. Only the pure `lastStatusAt` is unit-tested (tests/unit/panels.test.ts:114). Add a fixture awaiting approval with a status row and assert the wording and the <time>.

The review fetch moved from ReviewPanel into NodeDetail (src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx, key `${reviewPath}|${result_uri ?? status}`). decisions.md requires that 'a review opened before its verdict updates when it lands' and that an export without a link keeps its review, but no test opens a review node before its verdict and checks that it re-reads when node.status/result_uri change. launch-review-late (ux-launch.spec.ts:89) covers only the launch page's files, and live-refresh (projects.spec.ts:451) checks only the run status. Nothing guards the moved fetch or the rule that the sections do not fetch on their own.
findings.requirement: the sections never fetch or poll on their own and never call `useNow`

findings.message: decisions.md says 'No fan-out means no per-run detail request: every row renders from the run summary's served activity', but runs-home (tests/project-workflows/ux-lists.spec.ts:28-122) never watches network requests (no page.on('request') or route counter). A regression that fetches /runs/<id> detail per row would still pass. The request count appears only in prose in docs/handoff/ux-s6.md. The fallback wording for a row without activity is unit-tested (tests/unit/lists.test.ts:114-129), but no browser test renders such a row.
findings.requirement: The run page and the lists use the backend's served `activity` so waiting questions, pane attention and a stopped controller are visible without opening a run.
